narrative:
The model determined that you have a 37% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were your credit history, the loan amount you requested, and the length of the loan. Your credit history was the single biggest reason for the denial. Having a critical or other credits record pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk, even though this history is fairly common among applicants. The requested loan amount worked in your favor; at 2,820 DM it was slightly below the average amount approved applicants ask for, which helped pull the prediction back toward approval. However, the 36-month duration of the loan worked against you. This is almost twice as long as the average 19-month term among those who were approved, and it increased the model's concern about risk.

Taken together, the negative influence from your credit history and the longer repayment period outweighed the positive effect of the modest loan size, tipping the decision against approval.

You should focus on improving your credit history by paying all existing obligations on time and, if possible, reducing any outstanding debts. Once your record shows consistent, timely payments, reapply with a shorter loan term. This combination of actions will give you the best chance of a favorable decision in the future. (218 words)
